subject: science
passage: Below about 1,000 meters, the deep ocean receives no sunlight at all, and food is scarce. Many female anglerfish living there have a long spine on the head that ends in a glowing tip, lit by bacteria living inside it. The fish holds this lure in front of its mouth and stays almost perfectly still. Small fish and shrimp in the deep sea are often drawn toward points of light. The lure most likely helps the anglerfish ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: spot predators approaching from far away in the dark.
choices.B: attract prey close to its mouth without chasing it.
choices.C: warm the cold water that surrounds its body.
choices.D: avoid being noticed by other animals nearby.

explanation.why: Small fish and shrimp swim toward points of light, and the anglerfish holds a glowing lure in front of its mouth while staying still. The lure therefore brings food to the anglerfish instead of the anglerfish going after its food.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says nothing about using the light to watch for predators.
explanation.B: Correct. Prey drawn to the light come right up to the mouth of the still anglerfish.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The lure gives off light; the text never suggests it gives off heat.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A glowing light in total darkness draws attention; it does not help the fish hide.
